generic_sampling_rules.integer_primary_key: Sequential integers starting above the compact max PK; never NULL; unique per table.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_foreign_key: Copy uniformly from the parent table's full PK domain (compact plus generated); never NULL unless the column is nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in the column's range rule; deterministically include the boundary list and one step on each side before random fill.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_price: Uniform decimal in the column's range rule; deterministically include the boundary list and one step on each side before random fill.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real in the column's range rule; deterministically include the boundary list and one step on each side before random fill.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Weighted pool sampler: base literal appears at least once, every near-variant in the column's pattern targets appears at least once, remaining slots fill from the realistic pool; no batch 'x' suffixing.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Draw from a small realistic pool; near-duplicates allowed only where a pattern lists them; NULL only where the column is nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, generated rows include at least one NULL and a NULL share matching the compact DB share (0.0 here -> exactly one planted NULL per instance); NOT NULL and primary-key columns never receive NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: Only on columns listed with duplicates_for_distinct: 20-50% of generated rows receive a fresh in-domain value (new realistic string or new integer), never a blanket character suffix.
generic_sampling_rules.deterministic_prefix_priority: When a column has boundary values and tie values, the deterministic prefix (boundaries + ties) must fit within the generated row count n; if it does not, raise n or drop only the least-constrained values, never the tie values required by ties_for_order_limit.

instance_size_semantics: table_sizes_per_instance is the TOTAL target size of each instance table (compact rows plus appended rows). The compact DB has 6 Manufacturers and 8 Products, so the generator must produce max(0, target - compact_rows) genuinely new rows per table: 6 new Manufacturers and 12 new Products. rows_added must equal the appended count (6 and 12) and rows_skipped must be 0. An instance with zero appended rows for any table is a failure, not a success.

uncertainty: Revenue NULL share is 0.0 in the compact DB but the column is nullable; exactly one NULL row is planted per instance for Manufacturers.Revenue, and NOT NULL / PK columns never get NULL. No calculated columns, no date pairs, no nullable FK, no enum columns with <=12 distinct values. Comparison_boundary targets for Manufacturers.Code and Products.Manufacturer may be satisfied by preserved compact rows; the spec does not force them into generated rows. With 6 new Manufacturers and 12 new Products, all per-column patterns (duplicates_for_distinct 20-50%, like_near_variant base + every variant, comparison_boundary values, ties_for_order_limit TIE_MIN/TIE_MAX, group_sizes 1/2/>=3, and the planted Revenue NULL) are exercised; the deterministic prefix (boundaries + ties) must fit within the generated row count.
